newsitem.title: USA: Jury reaches verdict in Reynolds trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury reaches verdict in Reynolds trial.

text.p: Jurors have reached a verdict in the widely watched trial of a wrongful death lawsuit against R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co, a court official said Monday.

Lawyers for the two sides were being assembled at the Duval County Courthouse for the reading of the verdict. The family of smoker Jean Connor sued the tobacco company, allegeding it made a dangerous and defective product and negligently caused the death of Connor.
The panel of five women and one man deliberated for eight hours over two days before reaching the verdict.

Jurors were asked to decide whether Reynolds had negligently caused the death of Connor, a heavy smoker who died of lung cancer in October 1995. They were also asked whether the company had made a dangerous and defective product that contributed to her death.
The plaintiffs asked jurors to award punitive damages against the company. If they do, it will be the first time punitive damages have been awarded in a tobacco liability case.
The trial is in its fifth week.
